## Markdown

```typescript
function Markdown({ children, className }: MarkdownProps)
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | `string` | required | the source; rendered as a document, not flattened. |
| `className` | `string` | optional | added to the element's classes, beside the one the theme gives it. |

Render markdown as prose.

GitHub-flavoured, because that is what people write: tables,
strikethrough, task lists and autolinks. Raw HTML is **not**
enabled and will not be — `rehype-raw` in a surface that renders
text somebody else wrote is a script tag waiting to happen, and an
extension's frame has a CSP precisely so that it cannot.

**Also** [`MarkdownProps`](/docs/sdk/ui-react/reference-content#markdownprops).

## MarkdownInline

```typescript
function MarkdownInline({ text, name = "", limit = 320, className = "", }: { text: string; name?: string; limit?: number; className?: string; })
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | — | optional | the markdown to render as one flowing line. |
| `name` | — | `""` | the document's name, so a title echo can be dropped. |
| `limit` | — | `320` | characters to keep; the clamp is visual, and this bounds the work. |
| `className` | — | `""` | added to the element's classes, beside the one the theme gives it. |

Markdown rendered as one flowing line of text.

See the note at the top of this file for what it does to blocks and
why. `limit` bounds the work, not the appearance: the clamp is
visual, and a document longer than `limit` is cut at a word
boundary with an ellipsis.

## loadMermaid

```typescript
async function loadMermaid(): Promise<MermaidLib>
```

Mermaid, configured for the theme in force right now.

Mermaid is about 700KB, so it arrives only if a document has one;
the bundler caches the module, so asking again costs nothing.
Configured on every call rather than once, because the theme is
read when it is configured — a diagram drawn after a switch to
dark has to be drawn in dark.

## MermaidBlock

```typescript
function MermaidBlock({ source }: { source: string })
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `source` | — | optional | the text inside the fence. |

A mermaid diagram.

`source` is the text inside the fence. A diagram that does not
parse is shown as its own source rather than as a blank box: it is
usually a diagram somebody is halfway through writing.

## fenceInfo

```typescript
function fenceInfo(children: ReactNode): Fence | null
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | `ReactNode` | required | the `<pre>` a fenced block renders as; its `<code>` child carries the language class. |

The language on a fenced block, or null.

Null when the child is not a code element, or carries no
`language-` class — an unfenced block, or a fence with no language.
